title: Qdrant vector store uses HTTPS unexpectedly with host/port/api_key for self-hosted HTTP Qdrant
author: haojingcn

comments.author: antan2002
comments.body:
Hi @haojingcn ,

I'd like to work on this issue. Could you please assign it to me?

From my investigation, the root cause appears to be that `qdrant-client` automatically enables HTTPS when an `api_key` is provided and only `host`/`port` are passed. Since Mem0 currently forwards these parameters directly to `QdrantClient`, self-hosted HTTP Qdrant deployments can fail with `SSL: WRONG_VERSION_NUMBER`.

My proposed fix is:

1. Add an optional `https` field to the Mem0 Qdrant configuration and forward it to `QdrantClient`.
2. Preserve backward compatibility by keeping the current behavior when `https` is not specified.
3. Update the documentation and examples to clarify the difference between:

   * `host` + `port` + `https`
   * `url` (e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:6333`)
4. Add tests covering:

   * HTTP Qdrant with API key authentication
   * HTTPS Qdrant with API key authentication
   * Existing host/port configurations

This should allow self-hosted HTTP Qdrant instances to work correctly while maintaining compatibility with existing deployments.

Thanks!

comments.author: rehan243
comments.body: Ran into this exact thing with Qdrant at scale - we were hosting our own Qdrant cluster on K8s and getting those `SSL: WRONG_VERSION_NUMBER` errors left and right. Turns out, `qdrant-client` defaults to HTTPS when you pass an `api_key`, which isn't super intuitive. We ended up switching to using the `url` param instead of `host` and `port` to get around this. The `QdrantClient` constructor's behavior is what's causing the issue here - when you pass `host`, `port`, and `api_key`, it assumes HTTPS. I'd suggest exposing an `https` option in the mem0 Qdrant config or switching to `url` like we did. We've been running Qdrant v1.8.2 in prod with 100M+ vectors and it's been solid.
